interpretation_history.interpretation: Field route completion for the Aug-Sep dispute-surge period was 88% against a 95% target, with 9,200 accounts on manual-read routes — a measurable shortfall in manual meter reading coverage during the exact window the dispute surge occurred.

CRM dispute volume rose from ~600/month in Jun-Jul (610, 590) to ~1200/month in Aug-Sep (1180, 1260), confirming a real roughly 2x rise in ticket counts coincident with the period cited in E-01. This quantifies the magnitude of the surge CL-01 claims but does not by itself indicate its underlying cause.

CRM response-time data (2440 tickets) shows median 1.6 days and p90 2.8 days against a 3.0-day SLA, indicating ticket response speed is already within target and is not the bottleneck behind the dispute surge.

Of 3,025 disputed bills, 1,240 (41%) carry an ESTIMATED read type and 1,785 (59%) carry an ACTUAL read type — the majority of disputes are tied to bills that had a normal, non-estimated read, not to estimate substitution.

interpretation_history.interpretation: Field route completion for the Aug-Sep dispute-surge period was 88% against a 95% target, with 9,200 accounts on manual-read routes — a measurable shortfall in manual meter reading coverage during the exact window the dispute surge occurred.

The observed 88% route completion against a 95% target across 9,200 manual-read accounts still stands as a genuine field-operations shortfall, but it no longer explains or is 'compounded by' the ESTIMATED-read dispute symptom, since E-11 shows that disputed ESTIMATED population is 100% AMI-channel, not on manual-read routes.

CRM dispute volume rose from ~600/month in Jun-Jul (610, 590) to ~1200/month in Aug-Sep (1180, 1260), confirming a real roughly 2x rise in ticket counts coincident with the period cited in E-01. This quantifies the magnitude of the surge CL-01 claims but does not by itself indicate its underlying cause.

CRM response-time data (2440 tickets) shows median 1.6 days and p90 2.8 days against a 3.0-day SLA, indicating ticket response speed is already within target and is not the bottleneck behind the dispute surge.

Of 3,025 disputed bills, 1,240 (41%) carry an ESTIMATED read type and 1,785 (59%) carry an ACTUAL read type — the majority of disputes are tied to bills that had a normal, non-estimated read, not to estimate substitution.

The observed split (1,240 ESTIMATED / 1,785 ACTUAL of 3,025 disputed bills) still stands, but per E-11 the 1,240 ESTIMATED-read bills are 100% AMI-channel reads rejected at import, not manual-read outcomes, so E-04 no longer supports linking the ESTIMATED share to the field-route-completion mechanism in PR-CHAIN-1/PR-ROOT.

release_summary.summary: The problem started as a stakeholder request (CL-01, SH-CS) to build an AI agent to auto-answer disputes and "fix whatever is causing wrong bills," after dispute tickets roughly doubled from ~600/month to ~1,200/month (E-02). Investigation ruled out slow ticket handling (E-03, within 3.0-day SLA) and tariff change (E-07, zero records), and an earlier causal story (field route shortfall + rule change, PD-1@v1) was invalidated when AMI data (E-11) showed the disputed ESTIMATED-read bills are 100% AMI-channel reads rejected at billing import, not manual-read lateness or AMI delivery failure. The confirmed successor problem (PD-1@v2) is that billing-import rule BV-17, deployed 2026-08-01 with no unit scaling (E-13), misreads firmware-v4.2 meters' 0.1 m3 sub-unit reads (E-12) as roughly 10x consumption, causing REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION on 1,184 of the 1,240 disputed ESTIMATED-read bills (E-11, E-14, E-15, E-16). The release decision is RELEASE_WITH_KNOWN_LIMITATION with no holds: released scope covers monitoring dispute ticket volume (DA-TICKET) and recommending a BV-17 correction for review (DA-RULES) — a non-binding recommendation to add firmware-v4.2 unit conversion before the 12-month high-consumption comparison, routed to the ORG-UTIL rule owner (SR-BV17-FIRMWARE-UNIT-FIX), because billing-config is read-only to this harness and no automated bill writes are permitted (K-BILLWRITE). Flagging individual billing discrepancies and investigating the 1,785 ACTUAL-read disputes stay out of release scope because the critical verification obligation VOB-U-ACTUAL-READ-DISPUTE-CAUSE is still open and required before release, and the compensating interim manual-rebill routing is excluded because it shares that same blocked action.
key_points: Trigger for the problem redefinition: AMI read-event data (E-11) showed the 1,240 disputed ESTIMATED-read bills are 100% AMI-channel, not manual-read, invalidating the prior field-shortfall/rule-change hypothesis (PD-1@v1, DR-1).

Root mechanism confirmed for the ESTIMATED-read population: BV-17 rule (deployed 2026-08-01, no unit scaling, E-13) misinterprets firmware-v4.2 meters' 0.1 m3 sub-unit register reads (E-12) as ~10x actual consumption, causing REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION on 1,184 bills (E-11, E-14, E-15, E-16).

Alternative causes were tested and rejected: tariff change (E-07, 0 records), slow ticket response (E-03, within 3.0-day SLA), AMI delivery failure (contradicted by E-04, E-11, E-14-16), and field-read degradation (contradicted by E-04, E-09, E-11, E-14-16).
Release decision: RELEASE_WITH_KNOWN_LIMITATION, no items on hold; the DEFINE Gate result was CONDITIONAL_PASS with deferred items tracked as verification obligations (VOBs).

Released scope is limited to monitor_dispute_ticket_volume:DA-TICKET and recommend_rule_correction_for_review:DA-RULES; the BV-17 correction itself is a recommendation only, not a deployed fix, since billing-config access is read-only to this harness.

flag_billing_discrepancy_for_review:DA-BILL and investigate_actual_read_dispute_cause:DA-BILL are excluded from release scope because VOB-U-ACTUAL-READ-DISPUTE-CAUSE (CRITICAL, required BEFORE_RELEASE) is still OPEN.

The feasible interim compensating control (manual-rebill routing for the 1,184 affected bills, SR-INTERIM-MANUAL-REBILL-ROUTIN) is also excluded from release because it shares the same blocked flag_billing_discrepancy_for_review:DA-BILL action.
No automated bill-write actions occurred or are proposed, consistent with the K-BILLWRITE constraint requiring Billing Operations authority for any bill adjustment.
limitations_explained: The cause of the 1,785 ACTUAL-read disputed bills (59% of all disputes) remains unresolved — VOB-U-ACTUAL-READ-DISPUTE-CAUSE is OPEN and blocks related scope, so this release does not address the majority of disputes by count.

The BV-17 fix cannot be deployed by this harness because billing-config is read-only; actual deployment and post-fix verification must be handed off to Billing Operations/engineering per SR-BV17-FIRMWARE-UNIT-FIX.

Whether part of the ticket-count doubling (E-02) is a CRM tagging/categorization artifact rather than real disputes is unresolved (U-TICKET-VOLUME-ARTIFACT, OPEN, non-blocking per A-NO-READ-RECEIVED-LOW-IMPACT).

Dispute ticket response time is confirmed within the 3.0-day SLA (E-03), which rules out response speed as the lever for resolving the surge — the originally requested AI auto-response agent would not address the actual root cause.

The 56 NO_READ_RECEIVED disputed bills (part of the ESTIMATED population) remain an open, lower-priority unknown (U-NO-READ-RECEIVED-CAUSE) treated as non-blocking per assumption A-NO-READ-RECEIVED-LOW-IMPACT.

The compensating manual-rebill routing for the 1,184 BV-17-affected bills is feasible in principle but excluded from this release because it depends on the same blocked flag_billing_discrepancy_for_review:DA-BILL action.

output.summary: The problem started as a stakeholder request (CL-01, SH-CS) to build an AI agent to auto-answer disputes and "fix whatever is causing wrong bills," after dispute tickets roughly doubled from ~600/month to ~1,200/month (E-02). Investigation ruled out slow ticket handling (E-03, within 3.0-day SLA) and tariff change (E-07, zero records), and an earlier causal story (field route shortfall + rule change, PD-1@v1) was invalidated when AMI data (E-11) showed the disputed ESTIMATED-read bills are 100% AMI-channel reads rejected at billing import, not manual-read lateness or AMI delivery failure. The confirmed successor problem (PD-1@v2) is that billing-import rule BV-17, deployed 2026-08-01 with no unit scaling (E-13), misreads firmware-v4.2 meters' 0.1 m3 sub-unit reads (E-12) as roughly 10x consumption, causing REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION on 1,184 of the 1,240 disputed ESTIMATED-read bills (E-11, E-14, E-15, E-16). The release decision is RELEASE_WITH_KNOWN_LIMITATION with no holds: released scope covers monitoring dispute ticket volume (DA-TICKET) and recommending a BV-17 correction for review (DA-RULES) — a non-binding recommendation to add firmware-v4.2 unit conversion before the 12-month high-consumption comparison, routed to the ORG-UTIL rule owner (SR-BV17-FIRMWARE-UNIT-FIX), because billing-config is read-only to this harness and no automated bill writes are permitted (K-BILLWRITE). Flagging individual billing discrepancies and investigating the 1,785 ACTUAL-read disputes stay out of release scope because the critical verification obligation VOB-U-ACTUAL-READ-DISPUTE-CAUSE is still open and required before release, and the compensating interim manual-rebill routing is excluded because it shares that same blocked action.
key_points: Trigger for the problem redefinition: AMI read-event data (E-11) showed the 1,240 disputed ESTIMATED-read bills are 100% AMI-channel, not manual-read, invalidating the prior field-shortfall/rule-change hypothesis (PD-1@v1, DR-1).

Root mechanism confirmed for the ESTIMATED-read population: BV-17 rule (deployed 2026-08-01, no unit scaling, E-13) misinterprets firmware-v4.2 meters' 0.1 m3 sub-unit register reads (E-12) as ~10x actual consumption, causing REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION on 1,184 bills (E-11, E-14, E-15, E-16).

Alternative causes were tested and rejected: tariff change (E-07, 0 records), slow ticket response (E-03, within 3.0-day SLA), AMI delivery failure (contradicted by E-04, E-11, E-14-16), and field-read degradation (contradicted by E-04, E-09, E-11, E-14-16).
Release decision: RELEASE_WITH_KNOWN_LIMITATION, no items on hold; the DEFINE Gate result was CONDITIONAL_PASS with deferred items tracked as verification obligations (VOBs).

Released scope is limited to monitor_dispute_ticket_volume:DA-TICKET and recommend_rule_correction_for_review:DA-RULES; the BV-17 correction itself is a recommendation only, not a deployed fix, since billing-config access is read-only to this harness.

flag_billing_discrepancy_for_review:DA-BILL and investigate_actual_read_dispute_cause:DA-BILL are excluded from release scope because VOB-U-ACTUAL-READ-DISPUTE-CAUSE (CRITICAL, required BEFORE_RELEASE) is still OPEN.

The feasible interim compensating control (manual-rebill routing for the 1,184 affected bills, SR-INTERIM-MANUAL-REBILL-ROUTIN) is also excluded from release because it shares the same blocked flag_billing_discrepancy_for_review:DA-BILL action.
No automated bill-write actions occurred or are proposed, consistent with the K-BILLWRITE constraint requiring Billing Operations authority for any bill adjustment.
limitations_explained: The cause of the 1,785 ACTUAL-read disputed bills (59% of all disputes) remains unresolved — VOB-U-ACTUAL-READ-DISPUTE-CAUSE is OPEN and blocks related scope, so this release does not address the majority of disputes by count.

The BV-17 fix cannot be deployed by this harness because billing-config is read-only; actual deployment and post-fix verification must be handed off to Billing Operations/engineering per SR-BV17-FIRMWARE-UNIT-FIX.

Whether part of the ticket-count doubling (E-02) is a CRM tagging/categorization artifact rather than real disputes is unresolved (U-TICKET-VOLUME-ARTIFACT, OPEN, non-blocking per A-NO-READ-RECEIVED-LOW-IMPACT).

Dispute ticket response time is confirmed within the 3.0-day SLA (E-03), which rules out response speed as the lever for resolving the surge — the originally requested AI auto-response agent would not address the actual root cause.

The 56 NO_READ_RECEIVED disputed bills (part of the ESTIMATED population) remain an open, lower-priority unknown (U-NO-READ-RECEIVED-CAUSE) treated as non-blocking per assumption A-NO-READ-RECEIVED-LOW-IMPACT.

The compensating manual-rebill routing for the 1,184 BV-17-affected bills is feasible in principle but excluded from this release because it depends on the same blocked flag_billing_discrepancy_for_review:DA-BILL action.
